question.text: A Tax Information Exchange Agreement (TIEA) between two countries primarily serves the purpose of:

answer.text: Providing tax exemptions on cross-border investments between the two countries
Facilitating the exchange of tax-related information between the two countries to prevent tax evasion
Allowing taxpayers to choose which country they wish to pay taxes in
Replacing the DTAA provisions with a simplified flat tax rate on all foreign income

explanation.text: The Logic: A Tax Information Exchange Agreement is, by design, a narrow agreement between two jurisdictions whose sole subject is the exchange of tax-related information between their respective tax authorities. India enters into TIEAs primarily with jurisdictions where a full DTAA is not appropriate but where information sharing is needed to detect undisclosed foreign income, offshore assets, and other forms of tax evasion. A TIEA does not allocate taxing rights, grant tax relief, or set treaty rates. The Trap: "Tax exemptions on cross-border investments" is what DTAAs (and beneficial-rate articles within them) do, not TIEAs. "Allowing taxpayers to choose where to pay tax" is not what any international tax agreement does. "Replacing DTAAs with a flat tax rate" mischaracterises both DTAAs and TIEAs. Note: The cited NISM Series X-B Investment Adviser Level 2 workbook pages reviewed in the audit cover DTAA residence/source taxation, DTAA rates, TRC, and Form 10F, but do not define Tax Information Exchange Agreements or state their tax-evasion purpose on the pages checked. The framing above reflects general international-taxation policy knowledge.
